findings.title: include_website_name method (without ?) is dead code; website_name not in untrusted_attributes
findings.body: The serializer framework (ActiveModel::Serializer) looks for `include_website_name?` (with `?`) to determine if the attribute should be included. The manually defined `include_website_name` (without `?`) on line 153 is never called by the framework. It should either be renamed to `include_website_name?` (with `?`) or removed. Additionally, `website_name` is not in the `untrusted_attributes` list (line 105-111), so the auto-generated `include_website_name?` is not created. As a result, the `website_name` attribute is always included in the serialization (since `include_website_name?` is not defined, the framework includes it by default), which is inconsistent with the `website` attribute handling (which is in the `untrusted_attributes` list and hidden for TL0 users seen by anonymous). For TL0 users, the value would be nil, so it's not a privacy issue, but the inconsistency is a code quality concern.

findings.title: URI(website.to_s) is parsed multiple times
findings.body: The `URI()` parsing is done 2-3 times in the `website_name` method (lines 138, 143, 146, 149). It should be cached in a local variable to avoid redundant parsing on every serialization. For example: `uri = URI(website.to_s)` and then use `uri.host` and `uri.path`.

findings.title: NoMethodError if Discourse.current_hostname is nil
findings.body: The `elsif` condition on line 144 calls `discourse_host.split('.').length`, which would raise `NoMethodError` if `discourse_host` is nil (e.g., in a background job or rake task where `Discourse.current_hostname` is not set). The method should handle the case where `Discourse.current_hostname` is nil, e.g., by returning just the `website_host` or treating the nil case as a non-match.

findings.title: Missing tests for edge cases in website_name
findings.body: The tests only cover three cases: different domain (discourse.org vs example.com), same domain (example.com vs example.com), and parent domain (forums.example.com vs example.com). Missing tests include: URL with port (e.g., http://example.com:8080/user), URL with query string (e.g., http://example.com/user?foo=bar), URL with fragment (e.g., http://example.com/user#section), URL with encoded characters, URL with different protocol (https vs http), URL with subdomain of instance domain (e.g., blog.forums.example.com for forums.example.com), URL with subdomain of website domain (e.g., forums.example.com for blog.example.com), URL with nil website, and URL with invalid website.

findings.title: Subdomain matching logic may not handle all valid cases
findings.body: The `elsif` branch only matches when both hosts have the same number of parts AND more than 2 parts. This misses cases like `a.b.example.com` (4 parts) vs `b.example.com` (3 parts) where the website is a subdomain of the instance domain. The `else` branch's `ends_with?` check handles this case, but the logic is split across two branches in a non-obvious way. Consider simplifying the logic or adding a comment explaining the cases.
